answer: Picture a mesa where every agent must post a refundable bond before it may vote or earn. A new identity locks tokens for ninety days, and peers who catch it colluding can slash the deposit, broadcasting the evidence like a beacon to the whole network. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand bonds, all exposed to one shared failure. Reaching the summit of influence therefore costs real capital that grows with each sybil, while honest agents simply recover their stake.
